author: Al Jazeera English
description:
For 18 months, civilians in Sudan’s el-Fasher were trapped under siege as the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces surrounded the western city, cutting off food and escape routes. When the city fell in October, thousands were killed as people tried to flee.

Survivors describe civilians being shot on the roads out of the city with bodies left behind. Rights groups say the RSF’s campaign in Darfur appears systematic, raising concerns of ethnic cleansing. Satellite imagery shows an earth barrier encircling el-Fasher, further restricting movement.

Through survivor testimony and visual evidence, Fault Lines, Lighthouse Reports and the Sudan War Monitor reconstruct the siege and investigate allegations of mass killings, disappearances and other abuses.

Credits: 

In collaboration with Lighthouse Reports and Sudan War Monitor. 

Director and Producer: Amel Guettatfi 
Correspondent and Producer: Julia Steers
Editor: Adrienne Haspel
Executive Producer: Laila Al-Arian

title: Encircled, starved and killed: The siege of Sudan's el-Fasher | Fault Lines Documentary

The move further restricted maritime traffic in Strait of Hormuz where Iran has continued to block movement of most foreign ships.
Several skirmishes have been reported in the critical waterway since then.
Roughly 1/5 of global oil exports passed through the waterway before the conflict began.

Al Jazeera’s Almigdad Alruhaid has more from Tehran, Iran.

And 78 years later, the cycle of loss and mass expulsion is repeating itself.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Jenin refugee camp in the occupied West Bank.

description:
"Partners not, rivals" - those are the words of China's President Xi Jinping as he welcomed US President Donald Trump.
The US leader shared similar sentiments saying the relationship between the two countries is "better than ever before."
Xi is holding talks with US business leaders in a visit that is expected to be dominated by trade.
Earlier, the two leaders met in The Great Hall of the People after a pomp-filled welcome ceremony.
But thornier issues are also likely to be discussed, including Taiwan and the Iran war.

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu has more from Beijing.

description:
Analyst Harlan Ullman says Gulf states, including the UAE, are facing growing political discomfort as regional tensions rise alongside uncertain diplomacy with Iran. He argues that Israel’s military actions across the region are contributing to heightened sensitivity in Arab capitals, complicating efforts to manage broader security and diplomatic balances. 

Ullman suggests that current US-led negotiations with Iran may struggle to achieve a stronger outcome than previous agreements, while regional actors continue to navigate competing pressures. He also points to rising military posturing and uncertainty around key maritime routes, underscoring the fragile state of regional stability.
